messages.subject: Error with CRP sampling
parts:
Hello, 

With reference to the appendix of paper "Flexible random-effects models using Bayesian semi-parametricmodels: Applications to institutional comparisons" by Ohlssen 2007, I’d like to use the following code of WinBUGS in nimble. I am interested in calculating the number of clusters (K). 

#Working code in winbugs (Ohlssen et al 2007)

for( i in 1: M ) {  #M is the number of observations and N is truncated number of clusters

logit(rho[i]) <- theta[Z[i]]

y[i]  ~ dbin(rho[i],n[i])

Z[i] ~ dcat(p[])}

#Stick breaking

p[1] <- r[1]

for (j in 2:N-1) {p[j] <- r[j]*(1-r[j-1])*p[j-1]/r[j-1]}

for (k in 1:N-1){ r[k]  ~ dbeta(1,alpha)}

ps <- sum(p[1:N-1])

for(k in N:N)

{p[k]<-1-ps}

for(i in 1:M) {for (j in 1:N) {SC[i,j] <- equals(j,Z[i])}}

# total clusters K#

for (j in 1:N) {cl[j] <-step(sum(SC[,j])-1)}

K<-sum(cl[])

}#END

When I adapt the above-code to nimble and use Chinese Process instead of stick-breaking, I get this error “ sampler_CRP: Detected that the CRP variable is used in some way not as an index: SC[i, j] <- nimEquals(xi[i], j). NIMBLE's CRP sampling not set up to handle this case." Why this error happens? How I can calculate the number of clusters then? My non-working code is below (some prior specifications are eliminated to save space):

for( i in 1: M ) {#M is the number of observations and N is truncated number of clusters

logit(rho[i]) <- theta[Z[i]]

y[i]  ~ dbin(rho[i],n[i]) }

# Chinese process 

Z[1:M]~dCRP(alpha,size=M)

alpha ~ dgamma(1,1)

for(i in 1:M) {for (j in 1:N) {SC[i,j] <- equals(j,Z[i])}}

# total clusters K#

for (j in 1:N) {cl[j] <-step(sum(SC[1:M,j])-1)}

K<-sum(cl[1:N])

}#END

Many thanks,

Nellie

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Error with CRP sampling
parts:
hi Nellie,

We have some checks in place to make sure that the MCMC we set up is legitimate for a given model that uses CRP.
That checking is not smart enough to realize that what you are doing is just doing some deterministic calculations based on the Z[i] values.

Instead of calculating K inside the model, please remove the code 

```

for(i in 1:M) {for (j in 1:N) {SC[i,j] <- equals(j,Z[i])}}
# total clusters K#
for (j in 1:N) {cl[j] <-step(sum(SC[1:M,j])-1)}
K<-sum(cl[1:N])

```

Instead, just do the calculations with the output of the MCMC sampling in R, making sure to monitor 'Z'.

Let us know if you have questions or that doesn't work.

-chris
